content: This enforced shift to road transport, while temporarily mitigating rail-related delays, has introduced new supply chain challenges, including heavily increased operational costs and a subsequent reduction in competitiveness within global coal markets . Rail project developments frequently encounter complex challenges, including tariff uncertainties and persistent workforce gaps, which can indirectly constrain overall rail capacity and elevate operational costs [84] . Additionally, shared rail networks face competing pressures from passenger services; for example, record Amtrak ridership and extensive infrastructure planning linked to the upcoming 2026 World Cup highlight a heightened reliance on rail systems that could necessitate careful scheduling to avoid displacing freight capacity [85] . Against this backdrop of macro-level infrastructure variables, transport delays emerge as a critical factor that directly causes fluctuations and bottlenecks in processing schedules at toll washing facilities. Even minor disruptions in the rail network can cascade through the coal supply chain, forcing processing plants to idle during delivery gaps or scramble to manage sudden gluts of arriving material. Regional coal logistics present a mixed picture regarding network fluidity and delay management as of mid-2026. On one hand, updates from major carriers suggest localized improvements; a June 5, 2026, report from BNSF indicated positive performance metrics and improved coal network car velocities, pointing toward a degree of operational stability in specific corridors [88] . Conversely, other segments of the network continue to experience friction. Data from 2024 highlighted a notable trend in declining rail transport costs for coal moving from Northern Appalachia to West Virginia, with costs dropping from 16.78 USD in 2023 to 9.87 USD in 2024 [87] . While lower transport costs generally incentivize higher utilization of rail networks, they do not inherently insulate the supply chain from the physical delays and capacity constraints that disrupt toll washing cycles. Ultimately, the demand cycles for toll washing at Veralogix Plant Operations are highly sensitive to the operational realities of the rail networks that feed them. Infrastructure capacity sets the upper boundaries of what the processing facilities can handle, dictating peak throughput limits based on the volume of railcars the network can reliably deliver.
